briefdescription.para: Deprecated access to the text as a C string.

detaileddescription.para: Forwards to str().c_str(). The other buffer accessors of v5.0.1 (clear(), append(), and reserve()) were removed, since they allowed an application operator<< to alter the texts of the pending checks.

simplesect.para: A pointer to the null-terminated text.

detaileddescription.para: Forwards to str().c_str().

briefdescription.para: Deprecated test for an empty text.

detaileddescription.para: Forwards to str().empty().
Forwards to str().empty().

briefdescription.para: The check result, which formats its expression and its message.

detaileddescription.para: It assigns the buffer to the checks, retrieves and releases their texts, and uses the plain mode for the messages.

briefdescription.para: The plain text writer, for the names of the test cases and the operands of the application types.

detaileddescription.para: It uses the plain mode, which is private, to write the values in the names generated by test_each(), and, for append_operand(), the operands written by an application operator<<.

briefdescription.para: The maximum number of elements of a range written.

detaileddescription.para: Limits the size of the report of a check on a large container, which is held in memory (and, in TAP, copied) until reported.

briefdescription.para: The internal output buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Accumulates the formatted text; cleared by begin_check().

briefdescription.para: ANSI colour codes for output formatting.

detaileddescription.para: A reference to the colours of the owning reporter, so that later changes (e.g. enabling colours) are picked up automatically.

briefdescription.para: The check whose expression is in the buffer.

detaileddescription.para: Set by begin_check() and reset by end_check(); nullptr when the text in the buffer does not belong to a pending check.

briefdescription.para: The expression texts of the pending checks whose buffer was reused.

detaileddescription.para: Normally empty: a check is reported at the end of its statement, before the next check begins. Only when a check begins while an earlier one is not yet reported, as when the arguments of a check call a function that makes its own checks, is the text of the earlier check moved here, keyed by the check, so that the check objects themselves do not need to own a copy, which would increase the stack usage of the test functions.

briefdescription.para: Whether the formatter writes a message.

detaileddescription.para: Set only by the private constructor, used by check_result and by plain_text; in this mode the numbers have no type suffixes and no added decimal point, and the strings and the char values are not quoted.

detaileddescription.para:
colours
Reference to a colours instance for output formatting; it must outlive the formatter.
Initialises the colours_ reference with the provided colours instance. The internal buffer is default-initialised to an empty string.

detaileddescription.para: Writes the values as in the expressions of the reports, with the type suffixes, but without colours. Intended for the applications that test their own operator<< functions without a runner: construct a formatter, write a value, and compare str() with the expected text.

Parameters
None.
Refers to the colours_none set, so that nothing is coloured; the internal buffer is empty and the mode is not plain.

detaileddescription.para: Releases the internal buffer; the referenced colours are not owned.

briefdescription.para: Appends the string representation of a boolean value.

detaileddescription.para:
v
The boolean value.
Reference to this instance.
Appends the string "true" or "false" to the internal buffer based on the value of v.

briefdescription.para: Appends a character, as a quoted literal, to the buffer.

detaileddescription.para: The character is written between single quotes, with the non-printable characters escaped ('a', ' ', '\\0', '\\x1b'), so that it can be identified in the reports. To write a separator without quotes, use a string (" "). In the plain mode, used for the messages, the character is appended without quotes, and escaped only if it is a control character other than the tab and the line feed, or DEL.

c
The character to append.
Reference to this instance.
The character is written as a C++ character literal, between single quotes, by append_character(), so that the spaces and the control characters are visible, and a zero does not end the text when it is printed as a C string. The values above 0x7F (for example the bytes of the UTF-8 sequences) are written as two hexadecimal digits ('\\xc3').

In the plain mode, used for the messages, the character is appended as text, without quotes, and escaped only if it is a control character other than the tab and the line feed, or DEL, as append_plain() does for the strings.

briefdescription.para: Appends a UTF-16 code unit, as a quoted u literal, to the buffer.

detaileddescription.para: The value is written with the u prefix and the escapes of char (u'a', u'\\n'); the other values outside ASCII are written as universal character names (u'\\u00e9'), and the surrogates, which are halves of the pairs, not characters, as four hexadecimal digits (u'\\xd83d'). Without the overload, the value would be promoted to int and written as a number. The plain mode, used for the messages, writes it in the same way, since it cannot be appended unchanged.

c
The code unit to append.
Reference to this instance.
Written by append_character() with the u prefix, also in the plain mode.

briefdescription.para: Appends a UTF-32 character, as a quoted U literal, to the buffer.

detaileddescription.para: The value is written with the U prefix and the escapes of char (U'a', U'\\n'); the other values outside ASCII are written as universal character names (U'\\u00e9', U'\\U0001f600'), and the values that are not Unicode characters (the surrogates and the values above 0x10FFFF) as eight hexadecimal digits (U'\\x0000d83d'). Without the overload, the value would be promoted to unsigned int and written as a number. The plain mode, used for the messages, writes it in the same way, since it cannot be appended unchanged.

c
The character to append.
Reference to this instance.
Written by append_character() with the U prefix, also in the plain mode.

briefdescription.para: Appends a C string operand of a comparator.

detaileddescription.para: Quoted and escaped as a string view of the character type (with the prefix of the wide and Unicode strings); a null pointer is written as nullptr.

Char_T
The character type of the operand.
s
The operand.
Reference to this instance.
Appends the characters of the string, quoted and escaped as the overload for the string view of the character type does (without quotes in the plain mode, with only the control characters escaped), or "nullptr" for a null pointer, as the other operator overloads do for these values.

briefdescription.para: Appends the text held by an array of characters.

detaileddescription.para: Selected for the arrays of the character types, including the string literals, but not for the volatile characters, whose arrays are written as the pointers they decay to are. The text ends at the first null character or at the end of the array, whichever comes first, so that an array that is full, without a terminator, such as a fixed-size name field, is not read beyond its end. Otherwise it is written as the overload for the character pointers writes the text of a pointer.

Char_T
The character type; it satisfies detail::character, and is not volatile.
N
The number of elements of the array.
s
The array.
Reference to this instance.
The size of the array limits the characters read, so that an array that is full, without a terminator, is not read beyond its end.

briefdescription.para: Formats a logical AND as (lhs and rhs).

detaileddescription.para: A chain of ANDs, as built by all_of() for more than two operands, is written as a single group, (a and b and c).

Lhs_T
Left-hand operand type.
Rhs_T
Right-hand operand type.
op
The logical AND expression.
Reference to this instance.
The operands, written by append_and_operand(), are separated by the word and, in the colour of the result of each conjunction; a chain of conjunctions is enclosed in a single pair of parentheses, which are not coloured.

briefdescription.para: Formats an approximate comparison as lhs ~ (rhs +/- epsilon).

detaileddescription.para: The notation is the one used by Boost UT, in ASCII, so that it is also valid in the TAP output.

Lhs_T
Left-hand operand type.
Rhs_T
Right-hand operand type.
Epsilon_T
Tolerance type.
op
The comparison expression.
Reference to this instance.
Formats the operands of an approximate comparison as lhs ~ (rhs +/- epsilon), in the colour of the result, as the relational comparisons are.

briefdescription.para: Formats a relational comparison as lhs op rhs.

detaileddescription.para: The operator symbol is taken from the tag (for example == for detail::equal_to).

Lhs_T
Left-hand operand type.
Rhs_T
Right-hand operand type.
Compare_T
The tag that defines the comparison.
op
The comparison expression.
Reference to this instance.
The left-hand side and right-hand side values are formatted and separated by the operator symbol of the tag (==, !=, >, >=, <, or <= for the built-in tags, or the symbol of an application tag), in the colour of the result (green for passed, red for failed, when colours are enabled).
If an equality compares two ranges that are written truncated, the index of the first difference is appended, if the elements written do not show it (see append_first_difference()).

briefdescription.para: Formats a logical NOT as not operand.

detaileddescription.para: A negated comparison is written between parentheses (not (a == b)), so that the negation is not read as applying to the left operand only.

T
The operand type.
op
The logical NOT expression.
Reference to this instance.
Writes the word not, followed by the operand, in the colour of the result of the negation. A comparison is written between parentheses (see append_not_operand()).

briefdescription.para: Formats a nothrow expression as nothrow.

detaileddescription.para: If the check failed, the reason is appended (see append_throw_reason()).

op
The nothrow expression.
Reference to this instance.
Writes nothrow, in the colour of the result.
It is defined inline, not in the library sources, so that it is available to the applications built with exceptions even when the library is built without them.

briefdescription.para: Formats a logical OR as (lhs or rhs).

detaileddescription.para: A chain of ORs, as built by any_of() for more than two operands, is written as a single group, (a or b or c).

Lhs_T
Left-hand operand type.
Rhs_T
Right-hand operand type.
op
The logical OR expression.
Reference to this instance.
The operands, written by append_or_operand(), are separated by the word or, in the colour of the result of each disjunction; a chain of disjunctions is enclosed in a single pair of parentheses, which are not coloured.

briefdescription.para: Formats a unary predicate as symbol operand.

detaileddescription.para: The symbol is the one of the tag, written as defined by the application, so it includes the separating space.

T
The operand type.
Predicate_T
The tag that defines the predicate.
op
The predicate expression.
Reference to this instance.
Writes the symbol of the tag, followed by the operand, with the same colour highlighting as the logical negation, so that the predicates of the application are reported as the built-in expressions are.

briefdescription.para: Formats a throws expression as throws<TypeName>, or as throws when any exception is expected.

detaileddescription.para: If the check failed, the reason is appended (see append_throw_reason()).

Exception_T
The expected exception type, or void for any exception.
op
The throws expression.
Reference to this instance.
Writes throws, followed, when a specific exception type is expected, by its name between angle brackets, as returned by reflection::type_name(), in the colour of the result.

briefdescription.para: Appends the name of a named boolean constant.

detaileddescription.para: The constant, created by the _b literal, is reported by its name, not by its value, which is always true.

b
The named boolean constant.
Reference to this instance.
Appends the name as it is, without quotes, so that the comparison is reported with the name instead of true.

briefdescription.para: Appends a duration, as the count followed by the unit.

detaileddescription.para: The count is written without a type suffix, followed by the unit: ns, us, ms, s, min, or h for the standard periods, or the ratio, as [N/D]s, for the other ones. The overload takes part in the overload resolution only if the count is an arithmetic type.

Rep
The type of the count.
Period
The period of the duration.
d
The duration.
Reference to this instance.
Writes the count with append_number(), without a type suffix, then the unit selected from the period; the periods without a standard unit are written as the ratio, [N/D]s.

briefdescription.para: Appends the value of an optional, or nullopt.

detaileddescription.para: A value is formatted through operator<<, as the contained type, so an optional with a value is written as the value alone; an optional without a value is written as nullopt. The overload takes part in the overload resolution only if the contained type is printable.

T
The type of the contained value.
o
The optional.
Reference to this instance.
Streams the contained value through operator<< if there is one, otherwise streams std::nullopt.

briefdescription.para: Appends the members of a pair, as (first, second).

detaileddescription.para: Each member is formatted through operator<<, so the pairs stored in the maps are also formatted, as {(1, 2), (3, 4)}. The overload takes part in the overload resolution only if both members are printable, so that extension::printable is false for a pair that cannot be written.

T1
The type of the first member.
T2
The type of the second member.
p
The pair.
Reference to this instance.
Writes the opening parenthesis, the two members through append_elements(), and the closing parenthesis.

briefdescription.para: Appends the elements of a tuple, as (e1, e2, …).

detaileddescription.para: Each element is formatted through operator<<; an empty tuple is written as (). The overload takes part in the overload resolution only if all the elements are printable.

Ts
The types of the elements.
t
The tuple.
Reference to this instance.
Writes the opening parenthesis, the elements through append_elements(), and the closing parenthesis.

briefdescription.para: Appends a container's elements enclosed in braces.

detaileddescription.para: Elements are formatted as { e1, e2, … } by iterating the container and recursing through operator<< for each element. Only the first 16 elements are written, followed by ", ... (<count> elements)" if there are more; the elements of the types signed char and unsigned char are written as plain numbers, without the type suffix.

parameterdescription.para: A range type satisfying detail::formattable_range: with begin() and end() members or functions, not an array, not a string, without elements of its own type, and with printable elements.

briefdescription.para: Appends the value of a framework value wrapper via detail::unwrap().

detaileddescription.para: Only the wrappers with a get() accessor (the to_* wrappers and the literals) are accepted. Any other type satisfying extension::is_op must have its own overload, as the built-in expressions and extension::compare_op and extension::predicate_op have; without it, detail::unwrap() would return the expression itself, and this overload would call itself without end, so such a type is rejected at compile time.

T
A value wrapper type satisfying extension::is_op<T>, with a get() accessor.
t
The value wrapper.
Reference to this instance.
Delegates to detail::unwrap(t) to obtain the displayable value of a value wrapper, then streams it through operator<< to format it into the buffer. The get() constraint guarantees that detail::unwrap(t) returns the wrapped value, not the wrapper itself, which would select this overload again.
Iterates the container and formats each element separated by ", ", surrounded by { and }. Each element is streamed through operator<<, which recurses as needed for nested types.

Only the first max_range_elements_ elements are written; if there are more, the elements are still counted, and the text ", ... (<count> elements)" is written after the last one, so that a check on a large buffer neither exhausts the memory nor buries the report. The elements of the types signed char and unsigned char (such as std::uint8_t) are bytes, not numbers with a type, so they are written without the type suffix.
The range-based for statement uses the begin() and end() members, or, if there are none, the functions found by argument-dependent lookup, as detail::formattable_range does.

briefdescription.para: Appends a double value (no suffix).

detaileddescription.para: An integral value is written with a decimal point (42.0), to distinguish it from an int.

v
The double value.
Reference to this instance.
Converts v to its string representation via append_number() and adds the decimal point if needed (via append_decimal_point()), without a type suffix.

briefdescription.para: Appends a float value with type suffix "f".

detaileddescription.para: An integral value is written with a decimal point (42.0f); the infinities and the NaNs are written without the suffix.

v
The float value.
Reference to this instance.
Converts v to its string representation via append_number(), adds the decimal point if needed (via append_decimal_point()), and appends the type suffix "f", unless the text is an infinity or a NaN, which would read as a misspelling (inff).

briefdescription.para: Appends a long double value with type suffix "L".

detaileddescription.para: An integral value is written with a decimal point (42.0L); the infinities and the NaNs are written without the suffix.

v
The long double value.
Reference to this instance.
Converts v to its string representation via append_number(), adds the decimal point if needed (via append_decimal_point()), and appends the type suffix "L", the C++ suffix of the long double literals (there is no suffix "ld"), written in upper case, since "l" would suggest long. The suffix is not appended to an infinity or a NaN, which would read as a misspelling (infL).

briefdescription.para: Appends the text of a null-terminated C string of any character type.

detaileddescription.para: Selected for the pointers to the character types (char, wchar_t, char8_t, char16_t, and char32_t, possibly const), including the string literals when they are passed through a pointer; the arrays are written by the overload for arrays, which does not read beyond the array. A null pointer is rendered as "nullptr". The text must be null-terminated.

The char text is appended without quotes, with only the control characters other than the tab and the line feed, and DEL, escaped, in both modes, since this is how the string literals are written by the operator<< functions of the applications, for example for separators. The char pointers that are values to be reported, such as the operands of the comparators and the elements of the ranges, pairs, tuples, and optionals, are written quoted, like the std::string values, by the overload for basic_c_string; an application writes a quoted value with a std::string_view.

The text of the pointers and of the arrays of the wide character types is converted to UTF-8 and written as the char text is, in both modes, without quotes, so that the string literals of these types can be used by the applications, for example as separators. As operands of the comparators, these pointers and arrays are reported quoted, like the std::wstring values, by the overload for basic_c_string.

Pointer_T
The pointer type; it satisfies detail::character_pointer.
s
The C string, or a null pointer.
Reference to this instance.
The text is not bounded, so it must be null-terminated; the overload for the arrays is more specialised, so it is selected for the arrays, which cannot be read beyond their end.

briefdescription.para: Appends a signed char value, as a cast.

detaileddescription.para:
c
The signed char value.
Reference to this instance.
Converts c to its decimal string representation via append_number() and prefixes it with the cast (signed char), since the type has no standard literal suffix, and the suffix "c" would suggest char, which is written as a character.

briefdescription.para: Appends a signed int value (no suffix).

detaileddescription.para:
v
The signed int value.
Reference to this instance.
Converts v to its decimal string representation via append_number() without a type suffix.

briefdescription.para: Appends a signed long long value with type suffix "ll".

detaileddescription.para:
v
The signed long long value.
Reference to this instance.
Converts v to its decimal string representation via append_number() and appends the type suffix "ll".

briefdescription.para: Appends a signed long value with type suffix "l".

detaileddescription.para:
v
The signed long value.
Reference to this instance.
Converts v to its decimal string representation via append_number() and appends the type suffix "l".

briefdescription.para: Appends a signed short value, as a cast.

detaileddescription.para:
v
The signed short value.
Reference to this instance.
Converts v to its decimal string representation via append_number() and prefixes it with the cast (short), since the type has no standard literal suffix, and the suffix "s" would be that of the std::chrono::seconds durations.

briefdescription.para: Appends the string "nullopt".

detaileddescription.para: Selected for std::nullopt, so that an optional value can be compared with it (eq (opt, std::nullopt)).

Reference to this instance.
Appends the string "nullopt" to the internal buffer; also used by the std::optional template for the optionals without a value.

briefdescription.para: Appends the string "nullptr".

detaileddescription.para:
Reference to this instance.
Appends the string "nullptr" to the internal buffer.

briefdescription.para: Appends a string view to the buffer.

detaileddescription.para: The string is written between double quotes, with the control characters, the double quote, and the backslash escaped. In the plain mode, used for the messages, it is appended without quotes, with only the control characters other than the tab and the line feed, and DEL, escaped, since they can change the state of a terminal, or truncate a text.

sv
The string view to append.
Reference to this instance.
The string is written as a C++ string literal, between double quotes, by append_quoted(), so that the empty and blank strings are visible, and the control characters are escaped. In the plain mode, used for the messages, the contents are appended without quotes, by append_plain(), with only the control characters that can change the state of a terminal, or truncate a text, escaped (all except the tab and the line feed, and DEL).

briefdescription.para: Appends a UTF-16 string view to the buffer, as UTF-8.

detaileddescription.para: Written as the overload for std::wstring_view writes the text.

sv
The string view to append.
Reference to this instance.
Converted to UTF-8, and written as a std::string_view is.

briefdescription.para: Appends a UTF-32 string view to the buffer, as UTF-8.

detaileddescription.para: Written as the overload for std::wstring_view writes the text.

sv
The string view to append.
Reference to this instance.
Converted to UTF-8, and written as a std::string_view is.

briefdescription.para: Appends a wide string view to the buffer, as UTF-8.

detaileddescription.para: The text is converted to UTF-8 and written as a std::string_view is: between double quotes, with the control characters, the double quote, and the backslash escaped, or, in the plain mode, used for the messages, without quotes, with only some control characters escaped. The code units that are not valid, such as an unpaired surrogate, are written as the replacement character U+FFFD. The wchar_t units are taken as UTF-16 where wchar_t has 16 bits, and as UTF-32 otherwise.

sv
The string view to append.
Reference to this instance.
Converted to UTF-8, as UTF-16 where wchar_t has 16 bits, and as UTF-32 otherwise, and written as a std::string_view is.

briefdescription.para: Appends the hexadecimal address of a pointer.

detaileddescription.para: Null pointers are rendered as "0x0". Non-null pointers are formatted with snprintf using the p specifier.

The pointers to the character types are excluded, so that they are written as strings by the overload for the character pointers; the signed char and unsigned char pointers, usually byte buffers, are written as addresses.

T
The type pointed to, other than a character type.
v
The pointer value.
Reference to this instance.
The address is formatted by the detail::append_pointer() helper, shared with the detail::reporter.

briefdescription.para: Appends the underlying value of a scoped enumeration.

detaileddescription.para: The value is converted to the underlying type and formatted as that type, with its suffix (for example 1 for an int and (unsigned char)1 for std::byte, whose underlying type is unsigned char).
The unscoped enumerations are not selected, since they convert implicitly to an integer, and are formatted as one.
An operator<< defined by the application for an enumeration, for example to write the names of the enumerators, is preferred to this template.

T
A scoped enumeration type.
v
The enumeration value.
Reference to this instance.
Converts the value with static_cast to the underlying type, and streams the result through operator<<, which selects the overload of that type.

briefdescription.para: Appends an unsigned char value, as a cast.

detaileddescription.para:
c
The unsigned char value.
Reference to this instance.
Converts c to its decimal string representation via append_number() and prefixes it with the cast (unsigned char), since the type has no standard literal suffix.

briefdescription.para: Appends an unsigned int value with type suffix "u".

detaileddescription.para:
v
The unsigned int value.
Reference to this instance.
Converts v to its decimal string representation via append_number() and appends the type suffix "u".

briefdescription.para: Appends an unsigned long long value with type suffix "ull".

detaileddescription.para:
v
The unsigned long long value.
Reference to this instance.
Converts v to its decimal string representation via append_number() and appends the type suffix "ull".

briefdescription.para: Appends an unsigned long value with type suffix "ul".

detaileddescription.para:
v
The unsigned long value.
Reference to this instance.
Converts v to its decimal string representation via append_number() and appends the type suffix "ul".

briefdescription.para: Appends an unsigned short value, as a cast.

detaileddescription.para:
v
The unsigned short value.
Reference to this instance.
Converts v to its decimal string representation via append_number() and prefixes it with the cast (unsigned short), since the type has no standard literal suffix, and the suffix "us" would be that of the std::chrono::microseconds durations.

briefdescription.para: Appends a wide character, as a quoted L literal, to the buffer.

detaileddescription.para: The value is written with the L prefix, as a char16_t value where wchar_t has 16 bits (Windows), and as a char32_t value elsewhere (L'a', L'\\u00e9'); a negative value is written by its bits. Without the overload, the value would be promoted to an integer type and written as a number. The plain mode, used for the messages, writes it in the same way, since it cannot be appended unchanged.

c
The character to append.
Reference to this instance.
Written by append_character() with the L prefix, also in the plain mode. The value is first converted to the unsigned type of the same size, so that a negative value is not sign-extended to 32 bits.

briefdescription.para: Deleted copy assignment operator to prevent copying.

detaileddescription.para: The formatter is owned by a reporter and refers to its colours.

briefdescription.para: Deleted move assignment operator to prevent moving.

detaileddescription.para: The formatter is owned by a reporter and refers to its colours.

briefdescription.para: Returns the text written to the formatter.

detaileddescription.para: Intended for testing the application operator<< functions with a formatter constructed for this purpose; since the formatter only appends, the text of each value starts where the previous one ended. The text cannot be modified through this reference.

Parameters
None.
Const reference to the accumulated string.
Returns a const reference to the internal buffer_ string.

briefdescription.para: Constructs a formatter in the plain mode, for a message.

detaileddescription.para: Used only by check_result and plain_text, which move their text into the buffer, append a value, and move the text back, so that no other buffer is allocated. The plain mode writes the numbers without the type suffixes and without the added decimal point, and the strings and the char values without quotes, with only some control characters escaped; the messages are never coloured.

buffer
The text to which the values are appended.
Takes over the text of buffer, without copying it, refers to the colours_none set, and sets the plain mode.

briefdescription.para: Appends the operands of a logical AND, separated by and.

detaileddescription.para:
Lhs_T
Left-hand operand type.
Rhs_T
Right-hand operand type.
op
The logical AND expression.
Returns
Nothing.
The left operand is written first, as the operands of a chain if it is a logical AND too, then the word and, coloured by the result of this operation, and the right operand.

briefdescription.para: Appends an operand of a chain of logical ANDs.

detaileddescription.para: An operand that is itself a logical AND is written as the operands of a chain, without its own parentheses; any other operand is written as usual.

T
The type of the operand.
t
The operand.
Returns
Nothing.
The generic operand is written through the usual overloads.

briefdescription.para: Appends the text of a C string held in a buffer of a known capacity.

detaileddescription.para: The text ends at the first null character or after capacity characters, whichever comes first. A null pointer is written as "nullptr". The text is written without quotes, with the control characters escaped, in both modes; the text of the other character types is first converted to UTF-8. Shared by the overloads for the character pointers (unbounded capacity) and for the arrays.

s
The text, or a null pointer.
capacity
The number of characters that may be read, or std::string_view::npos if the text is null-terminated.
Returns
Nothing.
The text ends at the first null character or after capacity characters. It is appended as append_plain() does, with the control characters other than the tab and the line feed, and DEL, escaped, or as "nullptr" for a null pointer, as the basic_c_string overload does; the null pointer must therefore be checked before the text is read, and no more than capacity characters are read, so that an array that is full, without a terminator, is not overread.

briefdescription.para: Appends the text of a UTF-16 C string held in a buffer of a known capacity.

detaileddescription.para: As the overload for char, with the text converted to UTF-8 first.

s

capacity
The number of characters that may be read, or std::string_view::npos if the text is null-terminated.
Returns
Nothing.
Written as the overload for const wchar_t* writes the text.

detaileddescription.para: As the overload for char, with the text converted to UTF-8 first.

s
The text, or a null pointer.
capacity
The number of characters that may be read, or std::string_view::npos if the text is null-terminated.
Returns
Nothing.
The text, bounded by capacity as for the char text, is converted to UTF-8 and written as the char text is, without quotes, with the control characters escaped, whatever the mode.

briefdescription.para: Appends a character, or a code unit, as a quoted literal.

detaileddescription.para: Shared by the overloads of all the character types, so that they escape the values in the same way. The usual escape sequences are used for '\\0', '\\a', '\\b', '\\t', '\\n', '\\v', '\\f', '\\r', '\\'', and '\\\\', and the other control characters and DEL are written as two hexadecimal digits ('\\x1b'). The values that are not characters by themselves (the values above 0x7F of the 8-bit types, the surrogates, and the values above 0x10FFFF) are written with \\x and all the hexadecimal digits of their type, and the other values outside ASCII as universal character names, \\u with four digits, or \\U with eight. The printable ASCII characters are written unchanged. The hexadecimal digits are lowercase.

prefix
The prefix of the literal ("", "u8", "u", "U", or "L").
code
The value, converted without the sign extension.
size
The size of the character type, in bytes.
Returns
Nothing.
A value of an 8-bit type above 0x7F is a part of a multi-byte sequence; for the wider types, the surrogates (0xD800 to 0xDFFF) and the values above 0x10FFFF are not Unicode characters, and cannot be written as universal character names. They are written with \\x and twice as many hexadecimal digits as the bytes of the type, so that the width of the type is visible. The control characters keep the two digits of char, since they are the same in all the encodings.

briefdescription.para: Adds a decimal point to a floating-point value formatted as an integer.

detaileddescription.para: Called after a floating-point value was appended to the buffer; ".0" is appended only if the value was written with digits only, and not in the plain mode.

start
The position in the buffer where the value begins.
Returns
Nothing.
The shortest representation of a floating-point value with an integral value has no decimal point (42.0 is formatted as 42), so it cannot be distinguished from an integer. If the text appended since start contains only digits, after an optional sign, ".0" is appended. The text with a decimal point or an exponent, and the infinities and NaNs, are left unchanged, as is all text in the plain mode, used for the messages.

briefdescription.para: Appends the elements of a tuple-like object, separated by commas.

detaileddescription.para: Shared by the pair and tuple overloads; the elements are obtained with std::get<Is>() and formatted through operator<<, without the enclosing parentheses.

Tuple_T
A type accepted by std::get (a pair or a tuple).
Is
The indices of the elements.
t
The tuple-like object.
Returns
Nothing.
Expands the indices in a fold expression over the comma operator, so the elements are written in order; the separator is omitted before the first element. For an empty tuple, nothing is written.

briefdescription.para: Appends the index of the first difference of two ranges, if it is not among the elements written.

detaileddescription.para: A range is written with at most max_range_elements_ elements, so a difference after them is not visible in the report. The elements are compared in step, and, if the first difference is at an index not written, the text " (first difference at index <index>)" is appended. A range that is a prefix of the other differs at its size. Nothing is appended if the ranges do not differ, or if the difference is among the elements written.

Lhs_T
Left-hand range type.
Rhs_T
Right-hand range type.
lhs
The left-hand range.
rhs
The right-hand range.
Returns
Nothing.
Walks both ranges in step up to the first pair of elements that differ, or up to the end of the shorter one. The elements are compared as the comparator does, with equal_to::apply(), so that integers of different signedness are compared by value.

The comparison.

Returns
Nothing.
The comparison writes its own colours; the opening parenthesis is written in the colour of the negation, which is still active, and, since the comparison resets the colour at its end, the colour is written again before the closing parenthesis.

briefdescription.para: Appends the operand of a negation.

detaileddescription.para: Written as append_operand() writes it. A comparison, which has its operator between the operands, is written between parentheses, so that not (a == b) is not read as (not a) == b. The logical combinations write their own parentheses, and the predicates, written as a prefix, and the plain Boolean values do not need them.

T
The type of the operand.
t
The operand.
outer_colour
The colour of the negation, used by the overloads that write parentheses; ignored here.
Returns

briefdescription.para: Appends an operand of an expression.

detaileddescription.para: An operand that the formatter has a member operator<< for is written by it, unless the application defines a free operator<< for the type. An operand of an application type, found by argument-dependent lookup, is written in the plain mode, as the messages are, so that the values that its operator<< writes are shown as it writes them, without the type suffixes and the quotes; this includes the scoped enumerations and the types with begin() and end() for which the application defines an operator<<.

T
The type of the operand.
value
The operand.
Returns
Nothing.
The operands of the types that the formatter writes itself are passed to its operator<<; the other ones, the application types, are written by plain_text::append(), which hands to their operator<< a formatter in the plain mode. A type with a free operator<< is an application type, even if a template of the formatter accepts it too (a scoped enumeration, or a type with begin() and end()), since a call on this formatter would select the function of the application, which would write on the formatter of the report with its decorations.

op

Returns

briefdescription.para: Appends an operand of a chain of logical ORs.

briefdescription.para: Prepares the buffer for the expression of a new check.

detaileddescription.para: If the text in the buffer belongs to a check that was not reported yet (it was created by a function called in the arguments of this check, and is reported at the end of the statement), the text is first moved aside, so that this check can still report it. The buffer is then cleared and assigned to owner.

owner
The check that will format its expression next.
Returns

In the usual case, the previous check was already reported (its end_check() reset owner_), and the buffer is only cleared, keeping its capacity. Otherwise the text of the previous, still pending, check is moved into pending_.

Searches pending_ only when the buffer belongs to another check. If the check is not found (which does not happen when the calls are paired), an empty string is returned.

briefdescription.para: Prefixes a number with its type, written as a cast.

briefdescription.para: Formats values and expressions into an owned string buffer.

detaileddescription.para: expression_formatter owns a std::string buffer and provides operator<< overloads for all standard arithmetic types, character types, strings, pointers, containers, scoped enumerations (including std::byte), pairs, tuples, optionals, and framework expression types (see extension::is_op).

The numeric overloads append a type suffix (e.g., 42u, 3l, 1.5f, 1.5L) and write the types that have no standard literal suffix as a cast ((unsigned short)3); int and double have no suffix, and the floating-point values always have a decimal point or an exponent (42.0), so that they can be distinguished from the integers.

The same overloads also write the messages appended to the checks (expect (...) << value), so that a message accepts the same values as an expression, including the application types with an operator<< for this formatter. For the messages, check_result uses a formatter in the plain mode, which writes the numbers without the type suffixes and without the added decimal point (42, 1.5), and the strings and the char values without quotes, as text, with only the control characters other than the tab and the line feed, and DEL, escaped; the other values are written as in the expressions.
The class is non-copyable and non-movable to avoid accidental copying of the internal buffer.

Apart from the constructors, the public members are the operator<< overloads and the read-only str(), so that the application operator<< functions for user-defined types can only append text. The functions that assign the buffer to a check, and return and release its text, are private, and called only by check_result, a friend; an application function calling them would corrupt the texts of the pending checks.
